A sketch on a drafted face after the Draft's fixed plane changes (mitcad#2408, follow-up of mitcad#2351, GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#622), on the reported design (opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/draft-neutral-plane-reported-test.cmake): Extrude1 (F2) a 100 mm circle 40 mm high tapered -20 degrees, a cone; Extrude2 (F5) cuts a 40 mm wide slot from y = -20 along +y symmetric about the midplane Plane1 (z = 20), 10 mm each way, through the cone's side, its floor F5:end at z = 10; Draft1 (F6) turns the floor 5 degrees about its fixed plane, pulling along +y; Sketch3 (F7) lies on the drafted floor and projects its outline and the cone's section. The reporter drafted about the XZ plane, then changed the fixed plane to Plane2 (F8, the XZ plane offset 15 mm), as the design is saved: Sketch3 lost its plane and Redefine Sketch Plane did not take the drafted floor. The floor turned about the line y = p, z = 10 lies in sin(5) y + cos(5) z = 10 cos(5) + p sin(5); a sketch on a planar face has its frame's origin at the design origin's foot on the face's plane.
As saved: the floor drafted about Plane2 (p = 15). Every feature computes, the floor keeps its name, and Sketch3 lies on it.
Back to the XZ plane (p = 0), as the reporter first drafted it: the sketch moves with the floor.
The reporter's edit: the fixed plane changed to Plane2. The sketch follows the floor.
Redefine Sketch Plane takes the drafted floor: the sketch onto Plane1 and back onto the floor.
